section_summary.extract_value: This section reports testing a structural model (Fig. 1) using Mplus with maximum likelihood on a sample of N = 249, controlling for BMI and evaluating model fit with CFI, SRMR, and RMSEA. The authors trimmed nonsignificant paths, added a path from attachment anxiety to order perfectionism based on modification indices, and report that the final model accounted for substantial variance (e.g., 40.5% in body appreciation and 44.4% in intuitive eating).
section_summary.evidence_source: The number of participants (N = 249) exceeded the minimum 5:1 participants-to-parameter ratio needed to confidently examine a model (Bentler, 1990).; The structural model in Fig. 1 provided a good fit to the data (CFI=.98, SRMR=.04, RMSEA = .05), χ^2 (20, N = 249) = 30.61, p = .060.; Notably, a sizable percentage of variance (40.5%) in body appreciation was accounted for by restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, discrepancy perfectionism, and order perfectionism. Body appreciation, along with restrictive/critical eating messages and attachment anxiety, predicted 44.4% of the variance in intuitive eating.
